entries.clue: Some overhear trend in government is causing distress (5-7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken

blocks.note: sitting inside overHEAR TREND IN Government

annotation.surface: Someone complains that policy talk they have caught wind of in Whitehall is upsetting.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across four words, starting inside 'overhear' and ending on the first letter of 'government'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something heart-rending causes great distress or grief.

entries.clue: Drunk, Oscar tucked into beer – it’s the best part (4,5)

indicators.note: O is placed inside PINT, as a sheet is tucked into a bed

blocks.note: O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A tipsy drinker insists that the best bit of a night out is getting stuck into the beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an anagram signal, but here it simply means HIGH.
annotation.definitionFit: The high point of something is its best or most exciting part.

entries.clue: Fine everybody on the side of the Tories (3,5)

blocks.clueFragment: on the side of the Tories
blocks.note: the Conservatives (Tories) are the right-wing party in Britain

annotation.surface: A penalty for everyone who sides with the Conservatives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as a penalty but is the adjective meaning satisfactory. Tories is the everyday name for Britain's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Fine and all right both mean satisfactory or acceptable.

entries.clue: In North America, the home of the brave? (5)

definitions.text: In North America, the home of the brave?

blocks.clueFragment: In North America, the home of
blocks.note: reads as the start of the US anthem's closing line, pointing at the whole country
a brave is a young Native American warrior, so the setter wants the dwelling such a person lived in

annotation.surface: A line echoing the US anthem's 'land of the free and the home of the brave'.
annotation.walkthrough: The anthem phrase points at the USA as a whole; the question mark signals that 'brave' is instead the noun for a Native American warrior.
annotation.definitionFit: A tepee is the conical tent dwelling of Plains peoples, literally a brave's home.

entries.clue: Remainer and I hope rule must get changed (9)

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are altered in order

annotation.surface: A Brexit opponent hoping the rules will be altered.
annotation.walkthrough: A Remainer voted in the 2016 UK referendum to stay in the European Union, so is broadly a Europhile.
annotation.definitionFit: A Remainer, favouring EU membership, is a Europhile, an admirer of Europe.

entries.clue: Empty duke swallowing rum and large piece of cake (6)

indicators.note: DUKE with its inside removed leaves D…E
D…E takes ODD and L inside it

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A hollow-bellied aristocrat downing rum alongside a big slice of cake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning odd. Doddle is British slang for an easy task.
annotation.definitionFit: A piece of cake and a doddle are both something very easy to do.

entries.clue: Macron’s refusal to receive one cross old president (5)

indicators.note: NON takes I and X inside it

blocks.note: the French president would say non for no
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: The French president declines to take on an irritable former head of state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective describing the president, but it is the letter X.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Richard Nixon led the USA from 1969 until resigning in 1974, long enough ago to be 'old'.

entries.clue: Repeatedly drink and dance (3-3)

indicators.note: the word for drink is written twice

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

annotation.surface: A night of drinking and dancing, over and over.
annotation.walkthrough: Cha is an old British slang word for tea, borrowed from Chinese.
annotation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

entries.clue: Kind of car in ultimately dire condition (6)

indicators.note: take the final letter of 'dire'

annotation.surface: A car described as being in a terrible state.
annotation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
annotation.definitionFit: An estate is a type of car with a long body and rear door, a station wagon.

entries.clue: That man with styling product is a famous thinker (5)

annotation.surface: A man with slicked-back hair is hailed as a great mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Styling product' leads the mind to salons, far from German philosophy.
annotation.definitionFit: Georg Hegel was a German philosopher, one of the best-known thinkers of the 19th century.

entries.clue: Absurd notions of processions including farm animal (9)

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in as part of a whole, so PARADES holds OX within its letters

annotation.surface: Silly ideas about marches that include livestock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Absurd' could be an anagram signal, but here it belongs to the definition; the parades simply open up to let the animal in.
annotation.definitionFit: A paradox is a seemingly absurd or self-contradictory statement or idea.

entries.clue: Turn over headgear – small, medium or large? (7)

blocks.note: each is an example of a size; the question mark marks the definition by example

annotation.surface: A shop assistant hands over a hat and asks which fit is wanted.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as shopping for a hat, so 'Turn over' seems to mean hand it across; it is the boating sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A boat that capsizes turns over in the water.

entries.clue: European gets regular servings of not bad Italian dish (7)

indicators.note: take every other letter of 'not bad', serving it out at regular intervals

blocks.note: N o T b A d: the first, third and fifth letters

annotation.surface: A diner from Europe is given decent portions of an Italian meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Servings' fits the food surface while telling you to take letters at regular intervals.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category definition: cornmeal porridge from northern Italy, served soft or set and grilled.

entries.clue: Time chart I arranged to show activity for summer? (10)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone draws up a timetable for their summer holiday plans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who sums, and that person's activity is arithmetic.
annotation.definitionFit: Arithmetic, adding up figures, is what a summer (one who sums) does.

entries.clue: Record by medic is altered for medical problems (9)

indicators.note: the letters of 'medic is' are changed in order

blocks.note: an EP (extended play) is a record

annotation.surface: A doctor's notes are revised to reflect patients' ailments.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a medical file, but it is the vinyl kind, an EP.
annotation.definitionFit: Epidemics are widespread outbreaks of disease, serious medical problems.

entries.clue: Present wrapped by mother eagerly (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

annotation.surface: A gift enthusiastically wrapped by Mum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as a gift but is the adjective meaning in attendance, as in answering a roll call.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the roll-call sense: answering a register, 'present' and 'here' are interchangeable replies.

entries.clue: Caught in net at sea, did some fishing (9)

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of NET are jumbled

blocks.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

annotation.surface: A fisherman at sea hauls in a catch with his net.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a fishing scene, so 'Caught' seems to be part of it; it is the definition, meaning snared.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fish snarled in a net is both caught and tangled, which the fishing surface makes literal.

entries.clue: Cold-blooded killer working in Canada, surprisingly (8)

indicators.note: ON goes in with the letters of CANADA
the combined letters are rearranged in an unexpected way

blocks.note: on = working, as a machine is on

annotation.surface: A news story about a callous murderer employed in Canada.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'cold-blooded killer' sounds like a murderer, but it is a reptile.
annotation.definitionFit: An anaconda is a large snake, a cold-blooded reptile that kills by constriction.

entries.clue: What American sits on, nevertheless needing time (4)

annotation.surface: A question about what an American rests upon, still taking a while.
annotation.walkthrough: The butt is American slang for the backside, what anyone sits on.
annotation.definitionFit: In American English your butt is your bottom, which you sit on.

entries.clue: Following Harris’s lead, Biden gets confused (6)

indicators.note: the leading letter of Harris
to confuse is to mix things up, so the letters of H and BIDEN are mixed into a new order

annotation.surface: After Kamala Harris took over the campaign, Joe Biden is in a muddle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like the start of the scene-setting phrase, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the positional sense: whoever comes after in a line or race is behind, and the surface's succession story fits it too.

entries.clue: Loathed touring one Swiss city, and slept a long time (10)

indicators.note: HATED travels around I and BERN

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A traveller hated going round a Swiss city and slept through much of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Touring' fits the holiday surface while telling you to wrap one word around others; Bern, not Zurich or Geneva, is the Swiss capital.
annotation.definitionFit: Animals that hibernate sleep through the winter.

entries.clue: Dang it! Strangely, this is why people use Tinder (6)

definitions.text: this is why people use Tinder

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an odd way

annotation.surface: A frustrated swiper curses the apps people use to meet others.
annotation.walkthrough: Tinder is a dating app, not kindling here.
annotation.definitionFit: People use the Tinder app to find partners, that is, for dating.

entries.clue: Michael’s brief fuss in Gilbert and Sullivan role (6)

indicators.note: the short form of Michael loses its last letter

blocks.note: MIKE, the short form of Michael, cut short

annotation.surface: A man named Michael is making a small fuss about his part in a comic opera.
annotation.walkthrough: Brief works twice: Mike is already Michael's short form, and it is shortened again to MIK.
annotation.definitionFit: The Mikado is the title role in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado.

entries.clue: Hotel is dilapidated and unfriendly (7)

indicators.note: the letters are in ruins, knocked out of order

annotation.surface: A bad hotel review: rundown and unwelcoming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' tempts you to take H from the NATO alphabet, but the whole word is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and the surface's rundown hotel with surly staff shows the sense.

entries.clue: Dismisses revolutionary, a bit of a character (5)

indicators.note: revolving the word turns it back to front

annotation.surface: An eccentric radical gets the sack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' here is a printed letter, and a serif is a small stroke on it; 'revolutionary' seems to be a person but turns FIRES round.
annotation.definitionFit: A serif is the short cross-line at the end of a stroke of a printed letter, part of a character.

entries.clue: Chanel fan’s tropical tree (7)

blocks.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

annotation.surface: A fan of the Chanel fashion house has a favourite tree in the tropics.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The coconut palm is a tropical tree, often just called a coconut.

entries.clue: Approving cry from Fidel’s ex-comrade and queen (5)

blocks.note: Che Guevara fought alongside Fidel Castro

annotation.surface: A shout of support from Castro's old revolutionary partner and a queen.
annotation.walkthrough: ER is a crossword staple for the Queen, from Elizabeth Regina.
annotation.definitionFit: A cheer is a shout of approval or encouragement.

entries.clue: Make standard mineral so malleable (9)

indicators.note: the letters can be reshaped

annotation.surface: A metallurgist wants a uniform grade of a mineral that is easily worked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Malleable' fits the mineral in the surface, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: To normalise something is to make it standard or conform to a norm.

entries.clue: Many London stores stocking material, perhaps (5)

indicators.note: the phrase stores the answer inside it

annotation.surface: Plenty of shops in London sell fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stores' reads as shops, but it is a verb meaning holds; and 'stocking' is the garment, not the shopkeeping.
annotation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, famously used for stockings; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

entries.clue: Ronaldo fares badly in a wild-goose chase (1,5,6)

indicators.note: the letters are put together wrongly

annotation.surface: A footballer does poorly while chasing a hopeless cause.
annotation.walkthrough: Cristiano Ronaldo is a famous footballer, which makes 'fares badly' read as a match report.
annotation.definitionFit: A fool's errand and a wild-goose chase are both pointless, hopeless undertakings.
